items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: because I had this little trumpet player, Benny Harris, and he made some one nighters with me

ctx.x: Because when it first came out, I remember Hawk's reaction about this thing, and he said, 'Well, this is what I'm going to have to get with, you know, and he did, and, man, he could play it. But I still contend that you've got to know your instrument, and you've got to know the chord, something about it. You just don't play this by ear. Now you never did catch Red Allen, guys like that playing bebop. See? Gail Brockman was another guy, trumpet player, that, he played a little, but the fundamentals, man, you had…

And so I just decided to pass it up and not go that route. But I enjoy listening to it; even today I do, especially when the guys play it and it makes sense. I don't mean these little, young -- because I had this little trumpet player, Benny Harris, and he made some one nighters with me, and he played that stuff, man. And he would come behind that bebop and start swinging. And then he'd go back into the bebop, and he was versatile (inaudible), you know. That little cat could play, man! So I have nothing against…
Uh-huh. Was there much talk among jazz musicians at that time, you know, pro and con, or did it just --
